title: 6 Best Mattresses for Seniors in 2026: Firm Edges, Easy Exits
h1: The 6 Best Mattresses for Seniors in 2026
description: The Helix Midnight Luxe is the best mattress for seniors for most: a medium-firm hybrid with firm edges and a 12 to 14 inch height. 6 picks for sore joints.
dek: The Helix Midnight Luxe is the best mattress for seniors for most: a medium-firm hybrid with firm edges and a 12 to 14 inch height.
intro: A medium to medium-firm hybrid with reinforced edges and a responsive top layer is the right mattress for most seniors, because it is easy to sit on, easy to roll over on and still soft enough for sore hips and shoulders. Here are six worth buying and the specs that decide it.

Most mattress advice is written for a 30-year-old who sleeps through the night. A senior mattress has more jobs: it has to hold you up when you sit on the edge to put on socks, let you turn over without a fight at 3 a.m., and cushion an arthritic hip without swallowing it.
quickAnswer: the Helix Midnight Luxe is our #1 pick (best overall). The Helix Midnight Luxe is the best mattress for most seniors because it pairs reinforced edges and a tall 13.5 inch profile with a medium, zoned surface that cushions joints without trapping you.

blocks.p: The TEMPUR-Cloud is here because some people with arthritic joints simply prefer the deep cradle of memory foam, and Tempur-Pedic's material is the benchmark. It is a 10 inch all-foam bed; reviewers describe two 1.5 inch layers of TEMPUR material over a 7 inch polyfoam base. Tempur-Pedic calls the feel medium, and independent reviewers place it between about 5 and 6.5 out of 10. The cushioning at the shoulder and hip is the reason to buy it. The reasons to skip it are just as clear. Slow memory foam holds your shape after you move, so turning over and sitting up take more effort, and owners with limited mobility commonly report feeling stuck. With no coils, the edge compresses when you sit. At 10 inches it is also the lowest profile here, and dense memory foam is the most likely to feel warm. Buy it for a mobile sleeper who already loves memory foam, not for anyone who struggles to get out of bed.

sections.h: What Is the Best Mattress for Seniors?

blocks.p: Buy the Helix Midnight Luxe if you want one mattress that gets the senior basics right. Helix lists it at 13.5 inches with reinforced perimeter coils, zoned lumbar support and a medium feel it rates 6 out of 10. You get a firm place to sit and a surface that is easy to turn on.

For an even taller bed, the Leesa Sapira Chill Hybrid is 14 inches in three firmness levels. The Brooklyn Bedding Signature Hybrid offers Soft, Medium and Firm for less. The Purple Restore Hybrid is the easiest surface to move on.

The Nectar Classic Hybrid has the longest safety net, a 365-night trial and forever warranty. The TEMPUR-Cloud is the deepest cushion, and also the hardest to move on, so read its write-up before buying it for anyone with limited mobility.

Soft all-foam beds, collapsing pillow tops and very low mattresses are missing on purpose, because each makes getting out of bed harder. For every sleeper type, see our [guide to top rated mattresses](/best-mattress/).

sections.h: How Do the Six Picks Compare?

blocks.p: The table lines up the specs that matter most for older sleepers. Heights and firmness labels are the maker's own figures. Trial lengths are the brand's direct terms.
The four tallest picks all have coils that run to the edge, which keeps the side from folding when you sit. The two lowest have the most specialized feel.
The long trials belong to brands that sell direct, so where you buy matters. Buying on Amazon can change the terms, as the trials section explains.
None of these figures is our own measurement. Reviewers often place a mattress a point firmer or softer than its label, so use the trial to confirm the feel.

sections.h: Why Does Edge Support Matter for Getting In and Out of Bed?

blocks.p: Edge support is the most overlooked spec for seniors. Most people get up by sitting on the edge and pushing to stand. If the edge sags, you sit lower and tilted toward the floor, and standing gets harder.

blocks.h3: What a strong edge is made of

blocks.p: Good edges come from the coil unit: thicker perimeter coils, a foam rail, or both. Helix describes reinforced perimeter coils on the Midnight Luxe, Leesa reinforced side coils, and Purple edge support foam it says makes getting in and out easier.
An all-foam mattress has nothing stiff at the perimeter, so the edge compresses like the middle. That is the main reason the TEMPUR-Cloud ranks last despite its pressure relief.
On a weak edge, sleepers drift toward the middle. That matters for couples on a queen and for anyone who sleeps near the edge to reach a cane or a nightstand.
Heavier sleepers stress edges most; see our guide to mattresses for heavy people. During the trial, sit on the edge for a minute and check whether your hips end up lower than your knees.

sections.h: How Tall Should a Mattress Be for Seniors?

blocks.p: What matters is total sitting height: frame plus foundation plus mattress. A common guideline is that your feet rest flat on the floor with knees at roughly a right angle when you sit on the edge.
Measure from the floor to the seat of a firm chair you stand up from easily. That is a good target for the mattress edge. Your leg length decides, not a chart.

blocks.p: Swapping a 10-inch mattress for a 14-inch one raises the bed four inches. The Leesa and Helix are the tall options here; the Purple Restore and TEMPUR-Cloud suit frames that already sit high.
Do not overshoot. A bed that is too tall forces you to hop down, which is a fall risk. When buying for a parent, measure their bed and their best chair first.

sections.h: Responsive or Sinking Foam: Which Is Easier to Move On?

blocks.p: Ease of movement comes down to how quickly the top layer pushes back. A slow foam holds your shape for a few seconds after you move, so you are always climbing out of a dent.

Memory foam softens with body heat and recovers slowly. That gives deep pressure relief, and it is why owners with hip or knee problems commonly report feeling stuck. A thin memory foam layer over coils is much less of a problem.

blocks.h3: Responsive foam, latex and gel grids

blocks.p: Responsive polyfoam, latex and Purple's GelFlex Grid spring back quickly. The Helix, Leesa and Brooklyn list responsive foams in their stacks, and owners commonly describe the Purple grid as easy to shift on.
Pocketed coils add a push that helps you change position and stand from the edge. If moving in bed is your biggest problem, choose a hybrid and avoid anything described as deep-hugging.
One caveat: a very responsive bed can feel less cushioning on bony points. The fix is usually a medium rather than a firm, not a slower foam.

sections.h: What Mattress Helps Joint Pain and Arthritis?

blocks.p: Sore shoulders, hips and knees need enough give that they are not pressed hard into the surface, while the lower back still needs support. Too firm creates sore spots; too soft lets the hips sink.

Picks to look at
rows: Side, with shoulder or hip pain

blocks.p: Zoned coils are softer under the shoulders and firmer under the hips. Helix and Leesa both list zoned lumbar support, though zoning never replaces picking the right overall firmness.

A better mattress can ease pressure on sore joints. It does not treat arthritis, and persistent pain warrants a doctor or physical therapist. See our guide to mattresses for back pain and the [side sleeper guide](/best-mattress-for-side-sleepers/) for more.
THE RULE
Start at medium, then adjust with the trial.
If a supportive mattress still feels hard on the shoulders after a few weeks, a 2 to 3 inch topper is cheaper than a new bed.
Our [mattress topper guide](/best-mattress-topper/) covers which topper materials keep the surface easy to move on.

sections.h: Does the Mattress Work With an Adjustable Base?

blocks.p: Raising the head helps people with reflux or snoring, or who rest upright, and some use it as a halfway point before standing. Raising the knees eases the lower back for some sleepers.
The mattress has to bend without damage. Foam and pocketed-coil hybrids generally do; connected innersprings often do not. The picks here are 10 to 14 inches, a range most bases handle.

Helix lists its adjustable bases as compatible. Purple says the Restore needs a base tested to at least 750 pounds. Nectar sells the Classic Hybrid bundled with its base. Leesa does not state compatibility, so confirm first.

Some brands require specific support to keep the warranty valid. Brooklyn Bedding asks for solid support or slats no more than 5 inches apart. Read the support rules before putting a new mattress on an old frame or base, and keep both receipts.

sections.h: Will It Sleep Hot, and Can You Move It?

blocks.p: Many people sleep warmer with age, from hot flashes or medications. Weight matters for a different reason: someone has to unbox the mattress, rotate it and change the sheets, often on a tall bed.

Coils let air move, so hybrids generally run cooler than all-foam beds. Purple says its grid draws heat away, and Helix offers a GlacioTex cooling cover. Dense memory foam is the most likely to feel warm.
Helix lists the queen Midnight Luxe at 115 pounds, Purple the queen Restore at 114, and Leesa the queen Sapira Chill at 103. That is a two-person job, so pay for in-home setup if offered.
None of these is designed to be flipped, because the comfort layers sit on one side. Rotate head to foot every few months, and use deep-pocket sheets that are easy to change.

sections.h: How Do Trials and Returns Work, Especially on Amazon?

blocks.p: Direct trials here range from 90 nights at Tempur-Pedic to 365 nights at Helix, Leesa, Brooklyn and Nectar. Read the fine print for minimum nights and fees.

Purple asks for at least 21 nights before a return and deducts transportation charges. Tempur-Pedic charges a $175 return fee. The body takes several weeks to adjust to a new surface, especially with joint pain, so a long trial is worth more than a small discount.

A brand's trial may cover only direct orders. Tempur-Pedic says its trial excludes other retailers, and Leesa's Amazon listings mention 100 or 120 nights versus 365 direct. Check the seller and return terms first.

Warranties cover defects like deep impressions, not comfort. Helix, Leesa and Brooklyn list limited lifetime, Nectar forever, and Purple and Tempur-Pedic 10 years. Keep the law tag on, register the mattress, and photograph any sag with a straightedge in case you need to file a claim.

mistakes: Choosing the softest bed for sore joints

Very soft mattresses feel kind in the showroom, but the hips sink, the spine twists and the edge collapses. For most seniors with joint pain, medium or medium-firm on a hybrid cushions pressure points while still letting you move and stand. Add a topper later if it feels too firm.

A new mattress can change your sitting height by several inches. Measure the frame, foundation and mattress together, and compare it with a chair you can stand from easily. Too low makes standing hard; too high leaves feet dangling, which is a fall risk at night.
Buying deep memory foam for someone with limited mobility

Thick slow memory foam holds the body in place, so turning over and sitting up take real effort. Owners with hip or knee problems commonly report feeling stuck. If mobility is limited, choose a hybrid with a responsive top layer or a gel grid instead.
Assuming the brand trial covers an Amazon order

Some brands limit trials to direct purchases, and Amazon listings can show different trial lengths from the maker's own site. Tempur-Pedic, for example, applies its 90-night trial only to direct orders. Check who the seller is and read the return terms on the listing before you click buy.
Skipping the edge test during the trial

Sitting on the edge is the moment a weak mattress fails. In the first week, sit on the edge for a full minute, then stand up without using your hands if you safely can. If your hips sink below your knees, the edge is too soft for you.
bottomLine: For most seniors, the right mattress is a medium to medium-firm hybrid at 12 to 14 inches with reinforced edges and a top layer that pushes back. The Helix Midnight Luxe gets all of that right. The Leesa Sapira Chill is the pick for a bed that sits too low, the Brooklyn Signature Hybrid saves money, and the Purple Restore is the easiest to move on. Whatever you choose, measure the bed height before ordering, buy from a seller whose trial you have read, and use the first weeks to test the edge and how easily you turn over. If pain persists after the adjustment period, talk to a doctor or physical therapist before blaming the mattress.

faqs.q: What type of mattress is best for seniors?
faqs.a: For most seniors, a medium to medium-firm hybrid is the best type. The coils give a firm edge for sitting and standing and a bit of bounce for turning over, while the foam layers cushion shoulders and hips. All-foam memory foam beds offer deep pressure relief but are harder to move on and usually have soft edges.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress height for elderly people?
faqs.a: Aim for a total sitting height where your feet rest flat on the floor and your knees sit at about a right angle when you sit on the edge. Measure a chair you stand from easily and match it. Mattress thickness is one lever; the frame and foundation are the others, and they are often easier to change.

faqs.q: Is a firm or soft mattress better for arthritis?
faqs.a: Neither extreme. A very firm mattress presses hard on arthritic hips and shoulders, while a very soft one lets the hips sink and makes moving harder. Most people with arthritis do best on medium to medium-firm. Side sleepers usually want a touch softer, back sleepers a touch firmer. Persistent pain warrants a doctor or physical therapist.

faqs.q: Is memory foam bad for seniors?
faqs.a: Not bad, but often not ideal. Memory foam relieves pressure well, which helps sore joints, but thick slow-response foam holds you in place and can make turning over and getting up harder. A thin memory foam layer on top of coils, as in many hybrids, keeps most of the cushioning without the stuck feeling.

faqs.q: Can you put any mattress on an adjustable bed?
faqs.a: No. Foam and pocketed-coil hybrids usually flex well, but older connected innerspring mattresses often do not, and very thick mattresses can resist the hinge. Check that the maker lists adjustable base compatibility and any weight rating for the base. Purple, for instance, says the Restore needs a base tested to at least 750 pounds.

faqs.q: How often should seniors replace a mattress?
faqs.a: A commonly cited lifespan is seven to ten years, but replace yours sooner if it has visible sagging, if you wake stiffer than you went to bed, or if getting out of bed has become harder. Changes in your body matter too: a bed that suited you at 55 may be too firm or too low at 75.

faqs.q: What size mattress is best for an elderly couple?
faqs.a: A queen is the minimum for two adults, and a king gives each sleeper more room to move without disturbing the other. Couples with different firmness needs can use a split king, two twin XL mattresses side by side, which also lets each person use their own side of a split adjustable base.
